steps.what: Check documentation is present, readable and available in the driver's cab

tasks.design: Retain the check that required documentation is usable in the actual cab. A published copy in {DOCS} does not prove that the driver can access it there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Central publication and physical availability are different facts.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capture is needed to perform the existing check.
tasks.still_hard: Missing, damaged or inaccessible documents must be resolved locally.
tasks.human_edge: Verify usable access under actual working conditions.

evidence.claim: Document availability in a physical cab requires an actual access check; no saving is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is the driver's availability check, excluding document publication.
The document controller maintains the required document list through unchanged existing work. The driver produces availability observations in s1; no free inventory or offline-access flag is assumed.
Assess existing document facilities before additional software; no new tool is proposed.
Zero upkeep because this design leaves the process unchanged.
unknowns: Required documents and paper versus electronic provision
research_questions: Which failures prevent access despite central publication?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0 with zero upkeep; actual cab access still needs checking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Capture problems encountered and verify the relevant event facts
Prepare the incident narrative and required report fields

loop.purpose: Turn verified notes into a faithful report draft
loop.input: verified event brief and report template
loop.output: incident report draft with source references and unknowns
loop.check: Driver checks sequence, observed versus inferred cause, actions, omissions and uncertainty against notes
loop.stop: One correction pass then manual report if meaning remains unreliable
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied narrative accounts do not fit fixed field copying alone

steps.what: Correct and submit the exact report to the operator's safety team

tasks.design: Use the existing {OTHER} rail incident system's template before custom tooling. A bounded draft in {DOCS} uses the driver's verified event brief, and the driver approves the exact internal report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variable accounts require narrative assembly beyond a fixed form.
tasks.enabler_now: A source-bound draft can reduce prose preparation without deciding incident cause.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete recall, conflicting times and uncertainty about causation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish what was observed from what is suspected.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass writing; factual responsibility remains with the driver.

evidence.claim: The Dutch ILT describes company digital incident reporting; regulator filing is separate from the driver's internal report here.
Source-bound narrative drafting and the proposed saving are model-knowledge design assumptions, not a documented rail deployment.

assumptions: Boundary is the driver's internal report; emergency calls, operational response, investigation and regulatory filing remain separate and receive no saving.

The driver produces train identifier, event date, location, observed sequence, actions, approximate times and uncertainty in s1. Full capture and log comparison time remains; missing logs lead to manual entry marked unverified, never invented precision.
The safety officer maintains the report template; additional upkeep is counted. No free structured train-running feed is needed.
Test native forms and draft facilities before custom integration; no automatic cause classification or regulator submission.
unknowns: Existing incident system and report fields
research_questions: Does drafting reduce total report time while preserving uncertainty and chronology?

incremental.description: Template checks and sampled draft review

approvals.approved_version: Exact train, event chronology, locations, uncertainty and narrative snapshot; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R86 gross14 minus6 upkeep gives net8. Range0-3 allows rare incidents, conflicting logs or substantial corrections to absorb most gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor train loading procedures and intervene when damage risks appear

tasks.design: Retain on-site monitoring of loading and unloading. A work list in {OTHER}, the rail operations system, cannot establish that physical handling avoids damage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Risk emerges in the actual handling operation.
tasks.enabler_now: No supplied capability replaces live monitoring.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unstable loads or damaging contact in time.
tasks.human_edge: Coordinate immediate intervention with loading staff.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring time and authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: A planned loading record does not replace observation of physical handling.

assumptions: Boundary is the driver's monitoring, excluding loading staff labour and separate reports.
The driver observes condition and handling in s1; no pre-existing damage-risk flag is assumed. Loading staff work is unchanged outside the focal boundary.
Review installed tools before new software; no change is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no process or system is added.
unknowns: Loading method, freight and monitoring responsibilities
research_questions: What handling events require immediate intervention?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0; physical monitoring remains throughout.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less internal report drafting where verified notes exist; operating duties stay intact.
reach: Improve evidential handoff to safety colleagues
role.ambitious_version: A driver with clearer incident records and unchanged responsibility for operations.
